summary: Verified the hero logo swap from Logo_6_v2_Final@3x.png to active-recovery-360-logo.png. All 7 fix-in-place acceptance criteria pass. New image loads with correct src, natural dimensions 1071x384, mix-blend-mode normal, correct display heights (192px desktop / 144px mobile), proper alpha transparency (73.8% transparent pixels, opaque pixels are pure white forming letterforms), and no console errors on home. Regression pages load successfully.

verification_evidence.transparency_check: Corner pixel samples (top-left, top-right, bottom-left) all return RGBA [0,0,0,0] confirming true alpha transparency. Whole-image scan: 73.8% fully transparent, 21.3% opaque, and 100% of opaque pixels are white (>200,>200,>200) — meaning white letterforms on transparent background exactly as expected. No inverted-alpha white rectangle.
verification_evidence.visual_screenshot: Cropped logo screenshot shows crisp 'ACTIVE RECOVERY 360' letterforms with the blue hero background AND the athlete image visible around/behind the letterforms — confirming proper transparency and no residual white bleed.
verification_evidence.edge_quality: Edges appear crisp at both desktop (536x192 rendered from 1071x384 source = 2x retina) and mobile — no residual blur observed.

regression_pages./wholesale: loads; multiple 429 responses from rapid API calls (test artifact from consecutive navigations, NOT related to logo change)

critical_code_review_comments: home-page.tsx cleanly imports the new asset; drop-shadow filter is retained (subtle 2px shadow with 0.3 alpha) which is appropriate. No mixBlendMode, no imageRendering hint — matches spec.

The 429 rate-limit responses seen during rapid regression navigation suggest the backend has aggressive rate limiting on some API endpoints. Not a blocker for this iteration but worth checking rate-limit thresholds are user-appropriate.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 16 verified the final logo swap. active-recovery-360-logo.png (1071x384 RGBA) is loading with proper transparency, correct display sizes, and no blur. Bug is fully resolved. If further iterations touch the hero, re-run pixel-alpha canvas sampling to catch inverted-alpha regressions.
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration verified a fix, not a bug. Previous iteration 15 had upsampled the wrong-resolution PNG; iteration 16 replaces it with a properly extracted high-res 1071x384 RGBA PNG with correct alpha (source luminance -> alpha channel), yielding crisp, transparent-background logo rendering at retina density on both desktop and mobile.
